title: The Hard Extraction
premise: Rosalind Reyes, a private security contractor with a fabricated past and a permanently packed go-bag, receives a meeting invitation from her handler — sent twelve hours after his death. The invitation pulls her and her ragtag crew into an off-book extraction: spiriting a market-defector out of Frankfurt before opening bell, when the intelligence he carries could crater three economies. But the defector may be bait in a trap set by the very firm that trained Rosalind, and the dead handler's message forces her to confront the lie she's built her life on. Betrayed by her own employer and sheltered by the found family of her crew, Rosalind chooses truth over survival, burns her old identity to expose the conspiracy, and ends the book not running — but finally staying.
about_author: Petra Vasquez is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she was never allowed to name. She now writes thrillers from a small apartment overlooking a harbor, keeping one go-bag packed purely out of habit.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She runs a routine protection detail in Lisbon while cataloguing her exit routes, revealing her polished cover story about a dead sister and a quiet childhood. A junior colleague, Theo, notices she never unpacks. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours Dead
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her handler Marcus sends a calendar invite for tomorrow, 06:00 Frankfurt time — then his death notification lands minutes later. She verifies it's genuinely his account. Emotional beat: cold dread cracking through practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rosalind quietly recruits comms specialist Ines and ex-military driver Kofi, testing their loyalty without explaining why. Each says yes for reasons they don't fully admit. Emotional beat: the fragile mechanics of trust among people paid to distrust.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The team arrives to find the meeting point is a morgue viewing room; Marcus's body bears a note in his own handwriting: 'She knows what you buried.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into urgency.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They meet Dr. Lena Vogel, a quantitative analyst who stole proof that Rosalind's employer, Halcyon Risk Group, manipulates markets using stolen intelligence. Lena doesn't trust them either. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition of two liars.

chapters.title: Six Hours to Bell
chapters.summary: Kofi's POV. The extraction window tightens: Halcyon has flagged Lena's badge activity, and private contractors — Rosalind's former colleagues — are inbound. First firefight in a parking structure. Emotional beat: adrenaline masking doubt.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Rosalind's POV. Seven years ago she falsified an after-action report that got a teammate killed and bought her promotion. Marcus covered for her — and owned her ever since. Emotional beat: shame as the true go-bag she never puts down.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Holed up in a safehouse, the crew counts exits, ammunition, and lies. Theo catches Rosalind deleting messages and confronts her gently. Emotional beat: intimacy forming inside professional walls.

chapters.title: Halcyon Calls
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her director, Ambrose Vane, offers her a clean extraction for herself alone if she delivers Lena. He speaks to her like family. That's how she knows it's a leash. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging versus instinct of danger.

chapters.title: Lena's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She explains the scheme: Halcyon front-runs sovereign debt moves using intercepted diplomatic cables. Her data is encrypted, split across three keys, one held by Marcus — now dead. Emotional beat: conviction hardening into fear.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marcus's memorial page holds a steganographic image; Ines cracks it to find coordinates in Prague. Also finds a second file locked behind a question only Rosalind can answer. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling toward suspicion.

chapters.title: Question Only She Can Answer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The security question references the real name she abandoned. To unlock Marcus's file she must type the identity she killed. Emotional beat: the cost of remembering.

chapters.title: Prague Detour
chapters.summary: Kofi's POV. A tense border crossing with Lena hidden in a diplomatic courier case. Kofi shares why he left the military — a civilian casualty he can't undo. Emotional beat: two damaged people trading confessions at 130 km/h.

chapters.title: The File Opens
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Marcus's file contains evidence he was building a case against Vane for years — and a photo proving Rosalind's 'dead' sister is alive and working for Halcyon. Emotional beat: the floor giving way beneath her identity.

chapters.title: Sister, Alive
chapters.summary: Flashback interleave, dual POV. Rosalind recalls the sister she invented as cover — then realizes Marcus used the fiction deliberately, seeding it so she'd dig. Or did he? Emotional beat: paranoia as inheritance.

chapters.title: Tail in the Old Town
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A surveillance team shadows them through Prague; Theo runs a counter-follow that half-works, getting clipped by a car. First blood on the team. Emotional beat: guilt and grit.

chapters.title: Vane's Version
chapters.summary: Ambrose Vane's POV, first appearance inside his head. He frames everything as protection: Rosalind is an asset he rescued, shaped, loves in his own transactional way. He orders the team written off. Emotional beat: chilling paternalism.

chapters.title: Split Decision
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She proposes splitting: she'll meet Vane as bait while the others move Lena to the third key site in Zurich. The crew refuses to let her go alone; they compromise badly. Emotional beat: found family arguing like family.

chapters.title: Meeting the Maker
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Vienna sit-down with Vane. He reveals he knows about Marcus's investigation and offers her the thing she wants most: erasure of her past, a clean record, a new name. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Third Key
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In Zurich, the third key turns out to be biometric — Marcus's fingerprint, harvested posthumously by a notary he trusted. Ines realizes Marcus planned his own death's timing. Emotional beat: horror at a man who scripted everything.

chapters.title: Marcus's Last Move
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Decrypted video: Marcus explains he faked nothing — Vane killed him — but he arranged the dominoes anyway, choosing Rosalind because she's the only one Vane underestimates. Emotional beat: posthumous faith as burden and gift.

chapters.title: Betrayal Math
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Someone leaked the Zurich location; Theo audits communications and the evidence points to Kofi — or someone framing him. Emotional beat: suspicion poisoning the family they've become.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Limmat
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Team standoff by the river; Kofi proves his innocence by surrendering his comms rather than running. The real leak: Ines's encrypted client portal was compromised months ago. Emotional beat: forgiveness under fire.

chapters.title: Halcyon Closes In
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. He deploys the extraction team — including the woman from the photograph, Rosalind's 'dead' sister, now going by Mara. Emotional beat: Vane savoring the cruelty of symmetry.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She's real, recruited young like Rosalind, and believes Vane saved her too. She requests the assignment personally. Emotional beat: mirror-image longing, two sisters shaped by the same machine.

chapters.title: Siege at the Vault
chapters.summary: Action chapter, rotating POV. Halcyon hits the Zurich vault; the crew defends the decryption rig through a brutal close-quarters fight. Lena is taken. Emotional beat: loss amid competence — they fought well and still lost.

chapters.title: After the Loss
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Wounded, outgunned, down a principal. Theo suggests walking away; Rosalind, for the first time, refuses to run. Emotional beat: the go-bag stays packed but her feet stay planted.

chapters.title: Trading Places
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She contacts Vane offering a trade: herself and the decrypted ledger fragment for Lena. He accepts too quickly. Emotional beat: walking into the trap with eyes open.

chapters.title: Inside Halcyon
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Delivered to Halcyon's Frankfurt tower, she plays the repentant asset while mapping the building. She sees Mara across a glass wall. Emotional beat: recognition without reunion.

chapters.title: Sisters in the Glass
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Guarding Rosalind, Mara probes her about their shared childhood — which Rosalind invented. The fiction begins to feel truer than either woman's real history. Emotional beat: grief for a family that never existed, becoming one that might.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Live
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With Rosalind inside, Ines and Theo execute Marcus's contingency: pushing fragments of the ledger to financial journalists timed to Frankfurt open. Emotional beat: hope engineered under pressure.

chapters.title: Vane's Endgame
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. He plans to release a doctored ledger implicating Rosalind as the mastermind, sacrificing her to bury the story. Emotional beat: betrayal as house style.

chapters.title: Extraction, Reversed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She convinces Mara to help by showing her the real Marcus file — proof Vane ordered their handler's death and would burn Mara next. Together they extract Lena from holding. Emotional beat: the lie of sisterhood becoming its truth.

chapters.title: Tower Run
chapters.summary: Action climax part one, multiple POV. Escape through Halcyon's tower as alarms cascade; Kofi's driving, Ines's spoofing, Theo's nerve all pay off. Mara covers their exit and is wounded. Emotional beat: every skill earned across the book firing at once.

chapters.title: Open Bell
chapters.summary: Climax, Rosalind's POV. At 09:00 Frankfurt time the true ledger publishes; markets convulse; Vane's empire of foreknowledge collapses mid-trade. Confrontation with Vane in a stairwell where Rosalind chooses arrest over execution. Emotional beat: victory that costs the self she was.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Under immunity-for-testimony, she tells investigators everything — including the falsified report and the teammate's death. Full confession, no polish. Emotional beat: the lie finally put down.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Recovering in a hospital under witness protection, Mara must decide whether to testify too. She asks Rosalind to tell her a bedtime story about the sister who never existed. Emotional beat: chosen memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Unpacking
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Weeks later, the crew regathers at Rosalind's apartment. She unpacks the go-bag, item by item, narrating what each object carried. Emotional beat: quiet ceremony of staying.

chapters.title: New Client
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A stranger arrives needing protection — ordinary, frightened, unglamorous. The crew takes the job together, on their terms. Emotional beat: purpose rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: The Hard Part
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Rosalind's POV. Visiting Marcus's grave, she leaves the last item from the go-bag — his old lighter — and says the true name aloud for the first time in years. Walking back to the car where her family waits, she doesn't check the exits. Emotional beat: homecoming without escape routes.
